summary_short: Arjuna sees his relatives on the battlefield, becomes overwhelmed with sorrow, and refuses to fight.
summary_medium: Arjuna asks Krishna to position the chariot between the armies. Seeing his teachers, cousins, and loved ones on both sides, Arjuna is filled with emotional turmoil. His mind collapses under the weight of attachment, fear, and confusion. He puts down his bow, refusing to act. This chapter sets the stage for Krishna’s teachings.
summary_detailed: Arjuna asks Krishna to place the chariot in the middle of the battlefield so he can observe both armies.
He sees his teachers, cousins, grandfathers, and dear friends prepared for war.
Emotion floods Arjuna’s heart — attachment, fear, grief, and moral confusion.
His limbs tremble, his mouth dries up, and his Gandiva bow slips from his hand.
He feels deep sorrow at the thought of killing his own family members.
Arjuna’s emotional breakdown symbolizes the human soul facing impossible decisions.
This chapter shows how confusion, fear, and attachment weaken the mind.
It prepares the ground for Krishna’s wisdom in the next chapters.
what_you_learn: Why attachment is the root of suffering.
How fear can paralyze even the strongest person.
Why clarity is more important than strength.
The importance of seeking guidance when confused.
How inner conflict is the beginning of transformation.
